### [MemSteer: Turning User Histories into Supervision for Agent Memory Optimization](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39276>)

MemSteer generates evidence-backed questions and answers from user histories, checking answer plans through source audits and blind answer recovery. This supervision guides revisions to memory storage, retrieval and answer context without updating model weights, reducing reliance on manually labeled QA.

**Published:** 2026-10-29 · **First seen:** 2026-10-30T10:08:56.615+00:00 · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Agent Memory, Synthetic Supervision, Design Optimization

**Public availability:** 2026-10-30T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>) · [Timing source](<https://status.arxiv.org/>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.39276v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 3–4 and Appendix A: twenty design-search iterations raise ATM-Bench Question Score from 54.9 to 68.3 over 1,013 questions with DeepSeek-V4-Flash answering/judging. With GPT-4.1-mini, RHELM accuracy increases from 22.3 to 26.4 without external records and 33.3 to 39.9 with them. Generated supervision also helps two other optimizers.

**Limitations:** LLM verification can share errors and does not prove every cited record is necessary. RHELM uses ten synthetic personas; cross-user transfer is mixed. Official-QA comparisons include their own training/validation questions, whereas MemSteer reserves official questions for evaluation. No author implementation was verified.

## [2026-10-29](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Proactive Memory for Event-Driven LLM Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36967>)

ProactMem organizes an event stream into recent observations, source-checked activity trajectories and behavioral regularities admitted through historical replay. Matching those regularities to current conditions helps an agent decide when to offer assistance while suppressing redundant proposals.

**Published:** 2026-10-27 · **First seen:** 2026-10-28T10:04:45.988+00:00 · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Proactive Agents, Temporal Memory, Evidence Validation

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36967v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 3–5 and Appendices B–D: on 4,539 events from 17 isolated Sports/Home/Code streams, pooled F1 is 52.6%, 21.4% relatively above the strongest of five external baselines with GPT-5.6 Luna. Source-validation and replay ablations lower F1. Editorial catch-up from the October 28 screened reserve; the original paper announcement was October 28, not a new October 29 release.

**Limitations:** Method and benchmark were jointly developed without independent held-out evaluation. Separate-team labels lower Home/Code diagnostic scores, and controllers differ with memory representations. Offline opportunity detection does not measure recipient benefit, interruption cost or safety. Anonymous implementation contents and their earlier visibility could not be verified.

### [Benchmarks Are Surprisingly Compaction-Friendly](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31778>)

This study holds the agent harness fixed while varying when and how long conversations are compacted, then separately checks which user constraints survive. It shows why stable task scores can conceal lost instructions, motivating explicit constraint-retention evaluation alongside task completion.

**Published:** 2026-10-22 · **First seen:** 2026-10-26T10:04:55.340Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Context Compaction, Constraint Retention, Agent Evaluation

**Public availability:** 2026-10-26T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.LG/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.31778v1>) · [Project](<https://github.com/aisa-group/compaction>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. OpenCode experiments cover selected PaperBench, ProgramBench and PostTrainBench tasks with two valid runs per configuration. The two informative million-token models show little threshold sensitivity over 160K–380K tokens. Across 44 SWE-chat sessions and 269 extracted constraints, the main judge finds process/scope instructions dropped about six times more often than feature requirements. Original Monday cs.LG listing plus the official schedule supports inferred October26 00:00UTC announcement, preserving the October22 receipt.

**Limitations:** Few tasks, one scaffold and scores conditional on valid submissions limit generalization; PaperBench uses Code-Dev grading. Constraint judgments are model-based, and reward hacking starts before compaction, so erosion is not established as its cause. The author-linked repository is empty; no implementation release or independent reproduction is claimed.

## [2026-10-21](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-21.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Cache Engineering for Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28577>)

Cache engineering lets an agent drop selected KV states and reposition retained keys without rewriting its text history; AKV tracks operation history so shared or restored caches remain consistent. The full-paper study reports 1.7 points higher average task scores and 27.7% lower estimated token cost than threshold summarization across three models and four agent benchmarks, suggesting a useful route to context control when builders also control the serving engine.

**Published:** 2026-10-20 · **First seen:** 2026-10-21T10:02:45.248Z · **Novelty:** material-update · **Tags:** Context Engineering, KV Cache, Serving

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28577>) · [Code](<https://github.com/thu-nics/AKV>) · [Project](<https://fuvty.github.io/thinking_yard_project_page/projects/akv/>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Full Sections 3–5, Tables 1–4 and Appendices A.1–A.4 inspected. Drop changes future attention but not retained hidden states; repos rotates retained RoPE keys and resets future position indices, rather than making them equivalent to recomputing a shortened text. AKV uses operation-aware radix branches, drop-aware eviction and segmented restoration. Main policy retains the latest 12 tool responses plus reasoning, with model-specific position thresholds. Three-model/four-benchmark tests report mean 1.7 score-point gain and 27.7% API-equivalent agent/summary token-cost reduction versus Standard; costs exclude other tools and are not billed GPU expenditure. Eight A800-80GB BF16 GPT-OSS-120B serving replay reports 1.18 times output throughput and 1.51 times P95 request-latency speedup at each method's own peak concurrency. Original cs.CL October 21 batch plus official announcement schedule supports inferred formal-study availability2026-10-21T00:00Z. The September 28 repository and pinned October 15 README already document the drop/repos implementation but contain no benchmark results; this is proposed as the new full-paper evaluation/formalization over an older code preview, not as a newly invented operation.

**Limitations:** Cached hidden states retain information from previously attended dropped tokens, and arbitrary policies can degrade quality; serving support for linear-attention models remains future work. Serving replay selects 80 longest-context SWE tasks and replays recorded tool outputs with method-specific trajectories/budgets, not identical live workloads. API-equivalent prices and reposition charges are modeling assumptions. The current results-bearing project page is accessible, but its source repository/history returns 404, so earlier project-page visibility cannot be reconstructed and exact global first public visibility is uncertain. No independent reproduction.

**Update:** 2026-10-21: The first arXiv paper adds a formal operation-history account and a three-model/four-benchmark evaluation to the older AKV implementation preview. The verified October 15 README already describes drop/repos and compatible-cache reuse, so those mechanisms are not claimed as new on this date; exact earlier project-page visibility is unresolved.

### [Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20563>)

The authors periodically restart communicating research agents from their best candidate while clearing conversation and candidate histories, helping stalled searches explore larger changes. Across four code-optimization and model-training tasks, four-agent teams with this reset policy outperform their tested single-agent and independent parallel baselines at matched model spend, suggesting a practical memory policy for prolonged automated discovery.

**Published:** 2026-10-14 · **First seen:** 2026-10-15T15:09:00.000Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Agent Memory, Automated Discovery, Search Restarts

**Public availability:** 2026-10-15T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20563>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. October 15 new-submission listing and official schedule imply 00:00 UTC paper availability; submission was October 14 at 17:49:37 UTC. Full 14-page PDF, Sections 3–5, Tables 1–4 and Appendix B inspected, including visual checks of Tables 1–3. Pi/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, three runs per configuration: AHC014 mean best score is 1, 103k versus 964k for independent parallel agents. A same-state 30-proposal ablation gives communicating teams +9.2% after reset versus +1.4% on continuation.

**Limitations:** Four tasks and one model/harness; reset timing is fixed, not learned. Dollar budgets cover model spend rather than total experiment compute or elapsed time. Main comparisons combine communication and resetting; the same-state ablation better isolates resetting. No dedicated author implementation was verified, and results were not reproduced.

### [Pack Light, CarryOn: Building Object-Oriented Context for Long-Horizon Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18784>)

CarryOn organizes an agent's context around versioned reusable task objects, explicit unfinished obligations and a recent interaction tail, folding history only after evidence and consistency checks. This lets long-running agents continue from work already present in files or application state; matched Claude Opus 4.7 experiments improve OSWorld 2.0 partial score by 5.8 points while reducing total tokens by 51.9%, including context-management calls.

Matched OSWorld 2.0 partial score rises 43.9% to 49.7%, binary success 15.7% to 19.4%; 100 BrowseComp-Plus questions rise 49% to 56%.

Hippocam organizes ongoing work into nested intents, compressing completed work and older history while preserving original messages in a recallable tree. Recalled experience is consolidated again with new outcomes, allowing useful details and lessons to evolve without changing model weights.

### [RunningTab: Direct Workspace Interaction with Environment-Side Tabs](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10444>)

RunningTab maintains an external ledger of task requirements, captured file-reading observations and unopened candidate files while an agent works directly in a workspace. Requirement-focused review and a final completion check help the agent recover evidence that has left its context and identify missing parts of a deliverable.

**Published:** 2026-10-07 · **First seen:** 2026-10-08T10:03:51Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Working Memory, Evidence Tracking, Workspace Agents

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.10444v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Across three models and three workspace benchmarks, the authors report consistent gains over direct interaction and model-managed tracking. For DeepSeek V4 Flash, Workspace-Bench rubric pass rate rises from 53.28% to 59.99%, averaged over three runs; component ablations support the design. All methods share a 300-turn and one-hour task limit.

**Limitations:** The citation gate checks lexical overlap, not semantic correctness. Two benchmarks use restricted subsets, and the capture ablation also removes dependent review/evidence features. Equal turn limits do not establish equal cost; no public implementation link was located.

### [MemPilot: Orchestrating On-Demand Multimodal Memory Curation for LLM Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06830>)

MemPilot learns when to reuse compressed memory and when to ask another model to re-examine raw text or images for the current question. Jointly choosing evidence volume, processing instructions and model capacity provides a way to balance answer quality against memory-processing cost and modeled latency.

**Published:** 2026-10-05 · **First seen:** 2026-10-06T10:03:31Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Multimodal Memory, Adaptive Retrieval, Resource-Aware Policies

**Public availability:** 2026-10-06T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06830v1>) · [Code](<https://github.com/ViktorAxelsen/MemPilot>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The authors evaluate five memory benchmarks, including two held-out distributions, with separate downstream answer models and ablations of routing and reward credit. Reinforcement learning trains policies with different quality, monetary-cost and latency preferences; implementation and configuration files are publicly accessible.

**Limitations:** Reported latency uses a token-based proxy rather than measured deployment wall time, and cost aggregates questions per conversation history rather than per question. Filtered benchmark splits, model-based grading and one greedy trajectory per query constrain comparisons. Preference changes are evaluated through trained policies; the paper does not establish universal gains or a free runtime adjustment.

### [AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02163>)

AutoCompact trains a coding agent to decide when to summarize its history, preserve a useful working state, and continue consistently from that summary. Judge-corrected demonstrations followed by task-success reinforcement learning improve repository problem solving even when the original history fits in the context window.

**Published:** 2026-10-01 · **First seen:** 2026-10-03T10:03:03Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Context Compaction, Coding Agents, Reinforcement Learning

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.02163v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Three-run evaluations use one Qwen3-Coder backbone and a shared scaffold on SWE-bench Verified and SWE-PolyBench Verified, reporting 9.2 and 5.0 percentage-point gains over the base agent. Disabling compaction in the same trained checkpoint reduces performance, supporting a contribution beyond weight updates. Newly discovered in this run; its Oct 2 public announcement precedes the main window but falls within the 72-hour lookback.

**Limitations:** Evidence covers one model and coding tasks. Inference costs are token-price estimates excluding training and judge-guided data collection; summary-quality checks use keyword screening with manual spot checks. No code or checkpoint link was found in the inspected primary publication, and results were not independently reproduced.

## [2026-10-02](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-02.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Causal Memory Policy: Making Memory Utility Identifiable by Intervening on Retrieval](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02070>)

Causal Memory Policy randomizes a few retrieval slots so memories that the normal retriever misses can still have their effect on a specific answer measured. This provides a diagnostic for biased memory-utility estimates, while showing that accurate per-query measurements alone do not tell an agent what to retain for future questions.

**Published:** 2026-10-01 · **First seen:** 2026-10-02T15:33:55Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Memory, Causal Evaluation, Retrieval

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.02070v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Inspected the intervention design, estimator assumptions, benchmark comparisons and explicit limitations. LongMemEval experiments improve required-memory discrimination from 0.542 to 0.664 AUC, with additional analyses on LoCoMo, multi-hop QA and Mem0.

**Limitations:** The main identification demonstration uses a candidate pool constructed with knowledge of required memories; tested deployable selectors fail to recover that pool reliably. Exposure consumes context and the work makes no effective retention-policy claim. The linked anonymous code page yielded no readable content; not independently reproduced.

## [2026-09-30](../../../reports/2026/09/2026-09-30.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [ContextRender: From Execution Dependencies to Agent Context](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37743>)

ContextRender keeps complete tool results in a persistent graph and selects what the agent sees using observed value reuse, recency, and relevance. This gives long-running agents a way to reduce repeated context costs while retaining omitted information for later recovery, with competitive task performance under a 6K history budget.

**Published:** 2026-09-29 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T10:01:45Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** context-management, tool-use, long-horizon

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2609.37743v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Full methods, matched-budget baselines and ablations inspected; three models on AppWorld and 8-objective QA. Reports better task performance than five managed-context baselines across nine settings and 10.2–32.2% lower standardized inference cost than full history. The arXiv v1 submission was 2026-09-29T14:57:00Z, within the daily interval.

**Limitations:** Costs use a common pricing/cache model and only tasks triggering context management; they are not measured provider-bill savings. Performance is below full history in two settings. Reuse detection is exact, case-sensitive value matching; no independent reproduction or verified code release.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Effective context engineering for AI agents](<https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents>)

Anthropic describes a context-management approach that combines selective retrieval, conversation compaction, persistent notes, and separate subagent contexts. These patterns help long-running agents retain decisions and recover relevant information without carrying every prior observation in the active prompt.

**Published:** 2025-09-29 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Context Engineering, Memory, Long-Horizon

**Positioning:** established-method

The dated September 29, 2025 engineering article explains concrete implementations in Claude Code, including retrieving by lightweight references and preserving unresolved work during compaction. **Limitations:** This is engineering guidance with product examples, not a controlled comparison establishing the best memory algorithm. Compression can discard critical details, and runtime retrieval adds latency.
